note: malformed/bom-prefixed is valid/single-task's bytes plus a leading EF BB BF and nothing else, so it isolates Format.parse's BOM-tolerance branch: check exits 0 with the identical 'ok — 1 task parsed' line, list renders identically, and the BOM is dropped on the first write. Without it, an implementation that never strips U+FEFF passes every other fixture in the corpus while turning any BOM-prefixed store into 'missing meta record' plus an invalid-JSON error on line 1.

note: valid/delegation-closed-provenance carries the two closed-provenance cases the corpus lacked — an agent/claimed delegation on a DONE task and a human/delegated one on a CANCELLED task, both beside a `closed` date. It pins that Check forbids a delegation only on PROPOSED (so closure is not a reason to error or clear), that the open-scope delegation queries hide it while `--delegated --done` shows it, and that a write to a closed task re-emits the delegation in Delegation::KEY_ORDER, before `closed`. All nine pre-existing delegations sit on open tasks, so retention-through-close was previously unproved in either direction.

note: Two fixtures close the two halves the issue named. malformed/temporal-unknown-nested-key carries scheduled_time.precision and deadline_time.calendar_uid, pinning both unknown-key error messages and — against compat/forward-compat-unknown-keys' delegation, which warns and keeps — making NESTED_FORWARD_COMPAT's asymmetry visible as a class difference. valid/temporal-both-times is the only record in the corpus with all four temporal keys, so it is the single case that distinguishes KEY_ORDER's scheduled/scheduled_time/deadline/deadline_time interleave from a writer that grouped both dates before both time objects; every other fixture is byte-identical under both orders. Residue for oracle_gaps rather than fixtures_todo: no CLI invocation can observe the *drop* itself, because every mutation preflights Check against the whole file and this store fails that preflight (`task file is already invalid — run tasks check (nothing was written)`, exit 1, file unchanged). Format.dump_record's drop branch is reachable only at the unit level; the fixture pins the refusal that a port must actually reproduce.

Add to "What was found while building this" as a fourth numbered item:

**4. The temporal drop path is unreachable, and the store wedges.** `Format::NESTED_FORWARD_COMPAT` leaves `scheduled_time` / `deadline_time` out deliberately, its comment calling the next write the repair path for an unknown key there. That write never happens: `Check.check_temporal_time` makes the unknown key a hard error, and every mutation preflights `Check` over the whole file, so `malformed/temporal-unknown-nested-key` refuses every mutation with `task file is already invalid` and writes nothing. Reads still work. The only exit is a hand edit. A port must reproduce the refusal, not the comment.
